request: why does a sound get quieter as you walk away?

beats.intent: A speaker dot with sound spreading as circles of radius 1, 2 and 3
beats.narration: Sound spreads out from a speaker in every direction, like growing spheres.
beats.code:
stage.title("Quieter with distance")
src = Dot([-4, -0.6, 0], color=YELLOW, radius=0.15)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(src))
stage.add(src)
rings = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=r, color=BLUE, stroke_opacity=0.8).move_to(src) for r in (0.8, 1.6, 2.4)])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rings], lag_ratio=0.4))
stage.add(rings)
for r, t in zip(rings, ["1 m", "2 m", "3 m"]):
    stage.label(r, t, direction=UP, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: A small patch on each ring, the same sound spread over 4 and then 9 times the area
beats.narration: The same energy is spread over the whole sphere. Twice as far, the sphere has four times the area; three times as far, nine times.
beats.code:
patch = [Square(0.25, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to(src.get_center() + r * RIGHT) for r in (0.8, 1.6, 2.4)]
stage.play(*[FadeIn(p) for p in patch])
stage.add(*patch)
stage.caption("same sound, 1×, 4×, 9× the area")

beats.intent: Bars of loudness at 1, 2 and 3 m: 1, 1/4, 1/9
beats.narration: So the intensity falls to a quarter at twice the distance, and a ninth at three times.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [1, 0.25, 0.111], labels=["1 m", "2 m", "3 m"], color=ORANGE)
stage.equation(r"I \propto \frac{1}{r^2}")

request: how high up a wall does a 5 m ladder reach if its foot is 3 m out?

beats.intent: A wall, the ground and a ladder leaning from 3 m out
beats.narration: A five metre ladder leans against a wall, its foot three metres out.
beats.code:
stage.title("A ladder against a wall")
wall = Line([1.5, -2.5, 0], [1.5, 2.3, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=8)
ground = Line([-3.5, -2.5, 0], [2.5, -2.5, 0], color=GREY_B, stroke_width=4)
stage.play(Create(wall), Create(ground))
stage.add(wall, ground)
u = 0.9
foot = np.array([1.5 - 3 * u, -2.5, 0])
top = np.array([1.5, -2.5 + 4 * u, 0])
ladder = Line(foot, top, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(Create(ladder))
stage.add(ladder)
stage.label(ladder, "5 m", direction=LEFT, color=ORANGE)
base = Line(foot, [1.5, -2.5, 0], color=GREEN)
stage.add(base)
stage.label(base, "3 m", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The height up the wall marked h with a right angle at the foot of the wall
beats.narration: The ladder, the wall and the ground make a right triangle. The height up the wall is the unknown side.
beats.code:
hline = Line([1.5, -2.5, 0], top, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Create(hline))
stage.add(hline)
stage.label(hline, "h", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
ra = RightAngle(Line([1.5, -2.5, 0], foot), Line([1.5, -2.5, 0], top), length=0.3, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(ra))
stage.add(ra)

beats.intent: The picture beside h² = 5² - 3² = 16, h = 4 m
beats.narration: Five squared is three squared plus h squared, so h squared is sixteen: the ladder reaches four metres up.

request: if a bus comes every 12 minutes, how long do I wait on average?

beats.intent: A number line of an hour with buses at 0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 minutes
beats.narration: Buses come every twelve minutes: at zero, twelve, twenty four and so on.
beats.code:
stage.title("Waiting for the bus")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 60))
for t in (0, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60):
    mark_point(stage, nl, t, color=GREEN, label="bus" if t == 12 else None)

beats.intent: Three arrival times in one gap with their waits: arrive at 13 wait 11, at 18 wait 6, at 23 wait 1
beats.narration: You turn up at a random time. Just after a bus you wait nearly twelve minutes; just before one, hardly at all.
beats.code:
for k, (arrive, col) in enumerate(((13, RED), (18, YELLOW), (23, BLUE))):
    y = (0.6 + 0.5 * k) * DOWN
    d = Dot(nl.n2p(arrive) + y, color=col)
    w = Line(nl.n2p(arrive) + y, nl.n2p(24) + y, color=col, stroke_width=6)
    stage.play(FadeIn(d), Create(w), run_time=0.6)
    stage.add(d, w)
    stage.label(w, f"wait {24 - arrive}", direction=RIGHT if arrive > 20 else LEFT, color=col)
stage.caption("waits of 11, 6 and 1 minutes")

beats.intent: The line beside average wait = 12 / 2 = 6 minutes
beats.narration: Every wait from zero to twelve is equally likely, so on average you wait half the gap: six minutes.

request: how do tax bands work? Does earning more ever lose you money?

beats.intent: A bar of a £50 000 income split into a £12 500 tax-free part and a £37 500 part
beats.narration: Take a simple system: the first twelve thousand five hundred pounds is tax free, and the rest is taxed at twenty percent.
beats.code:
stage.title("Tax bands")
k = 0.16
free = Rectangle(width=12.5 * k, height=0.9, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([-5.5 + 12.5 * k / 2, 0.5, 0])
rest = Rectangle(width=37.5 * k, height=0.9, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(free, RIGHT, buff=0)
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(free, LEFT))
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(rest, LEFT))
stage.add(free, rest)
stage.label(free, "£12 500 at 0%", direction=UP, color=GREEN)
stage.label(rest, "£37 500 at 20%", direction=UP, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: A thin slice of the blue part lit as the £7 500 of tax
beats.narration: Only the part above the threshold is taxed: twenty percent of thirty seven thousand five hundred is seven thousand five hundred.
beats.code:
tax = Rectangle(width=7.5 * k, height=0.9, stroke_width=0, fill_color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).align_to(rest, RIGHT).align_to(rest, DOWN)
stage.play(FadeIn(tax))
stage.add(tax)
stage.label(tax, "tax £7 500", direction=DOWN, color=RED)
stage.equation(r"0.2 \times 37\,500 = 7\,500")

beats.intent: A raise of £1 000 adding a slice of which only £200 is tax
beats.narration: Earn a thousand more and only that extra thousand is taxed at the higher rate: you keep eight hundred. A raise never lowers your take-home pay.
beats.code:
extra = Rectangle(width=1.0 * k * 1.0, height=0.9, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(rest, RIGHT, buff=0)
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(extra, LEFT))
stage.add(extra)
stage.caption("+£1 000 earned: +£800 kept")
